   184	
   185	Three things are out of reach for a pure browser mesh regardless of plan quality, and all three resolve with
   186	the same component — an **operator-run node**, untrusted for state (bytes verified, cuts QC-checked, referee
   187	ops signed and disputable):

   189	1. **Ephemeral fanout above ~16 players/zone.** A browser cannot originate 30 Hz × 63-peer upload fanout.
   190	   Interest management reduces _relevance_, not the sender's fanout. An SFU-style relay is required.

   192	   configured hard safety limit"_ — reintroduces unbounded history exactly when quorum churns. At the
   193	   default `maxEpochVertices = 8192` and a modest 5 durable ops/s that is ~27 minutes to the hard limit.
   194	   Browser tabs also have a _negative_ incentive to sign (burn battery for closes benefiting latecomers)
   195	   and get OS-suspended.
   196	3. **Contested-outcome validity.** Attributability without a referee is not anti-cheat.

   199	complete origin-storage eviction** (§Phase 5) — so browser tabs cannot be **seal voters** by default.

   201	never-vote-twice slot obligation, and two routes let a browser hold it anyway: at `q = 1`, a recoverable

   203	`q = 1` _is_ a QC and lives on in the network); at quorum `≥ 2`, every voter preserves exact-slot
   204	anti-equivocation continuity through either detectable-loss durable storage, an external exact-slot
   205	witness, or — for a browser-local eviction-prone voter without such a witness — a **fate-shared
   206	non-extractable key** co-evicted with the vote log (§Phase 5, custody options 1–3). Trust profile determines
   207	authority and quorum; storage class determines custody. Both delegated and attested sets admit durable and
   208	browser-local voters. The liveness cost of fate-sharing is why an always-on durable-class signer remains
   209	in the picture as a **liveness backstop, not a trust requirement**.

   211	**Optional desktop clients are the P2P route to a durable tier.** If the product ships an **Electron
   212	build alongside the web app** — optional, opt-in, never required — any participant running it is
   213	durable-class by construction: no ITP, no 7-day clock, storage in the app's own data directory rather than
   214	a browser profile competing with a thousand origins. One such participant collapses **two of the three
   215	operator roles onto a peer**: signer (durable vote log) and mirror (it has a disk). Only **relay** does not

   243	## 1. Principles
   244	
   245	1. **Freeze before you port.** No consensus byte is written before the Phase −1 registry is merged. One
   246	   immutable golden-vector document is minted per registry version. Before reference regeneration, the only
   247	   lawful extension is an exact `registryVersion + 1` transition with exactly one new vector document that
   248	   carries every prior vector record byte-identically. Regeneration closes that window; any later consensus
   249	   change requires `protocolMajor: 3`. A vector diff must be impossible to land silently.
   250	2. **Compaction amplifies divergence.** The determinism foundation gates every snapshot-trusting feature.
   251	3. **Classify every change.** _replica-local-safe_ (ship now, legacy plane) / _coordinated-upgrade_
   252	   (observable post-merge state or wire format; test cross-version explicitly) / _consensus-affecting_
   253	   (**exactly one frozen protocol-major namespace, never patched in place, never dual-preimage under one
   254	   `objectId`; v2 remains immutable and v3 is its successor**).
   255	   A misclassification is a silent permanent fork — and round 1 misclassified three of its own slices (§Phase 0).
   256	4. **Every gate names an executable evidence artifact** — a test file, a model output, a crash-injection
   257	   log, a browser-matrix JSON, a golden-vector file. No inherited number is a gate.
   258	5. **Every gate must be provably able to fail — and a RED spec is evidence only as a pair _(baseline, current)_.** Before its GREEN half begins, every new RED spec file is executed against the baseline SHA in a throwaway git worktree (**never** `git stash` — reviewers share one tree), and the pair is recorded with the text of the failing assertion; a bare count is satisfiable by a broken harness. `FAIL/FAIL` is a genuine RED contract; `PASS/FAIL` is a **regression pin**; `PASS/PASS` is **not a gate** and must be strengthened or deleted; `FAIL/PASS` is already green. _Scope qualifier:_ the baseline leg binds only where the subject code exists at baseline — for `protocol-v2`, `seal`, `storage-browser` and the other new packages a baseline run fails on module resolution, and **an import error is not a RED**; there, run the spec before the implementation exists and record that it fails on the asserted contract. A regression pin must assert the **invariant**, never the baseline's behaviour: pinning the old semantics as a "positive control" makes the pin unsatisfiable alongside the slice that changes them (D.5(i)). Each differential/oracle gate additionally ships a **mutation probe**:
   259	   a seeded defect the gate must catch. The repo already has this pattern
   260	   (`packages/object/tests/proptest/mutation-check.test.ts`); it is the only known defense against an oracle
   261	   drifting green.
   262	6. **Every zero/never assertion ships a positive control** in the same test. _"Zero durable vertices"_
   263	   passes trivially if nothing is wired; assert in the same run that a durable command **does** create
   264	   exactly one vertex.
   265	7. **Atomic vs sliceable is explicit and argued — and every "atomic" names its observable boundary.**
   266	   For the legacy applier that boundary is _one vertex_ across **all** of: hashgraph (vertices, forward and
   267	   backward edges, frontier membership **and frontier order**, which feeds default dependency order and
   268	   therefore signed bytes), per-hash state snapshots, the finality store, the live `drp`/`acl` proxies,
   269	   `checkpoints`, `knownInvalidVertexHashes`, and subscriber notification. Two invariants come with it: the
   270	   owner stores are never rebound (identity is stable), and nothing is published before it is committed.
   271	   Atomic: the registry freeze itself; vertex preimage;
   272	   canonical-order switch; staged state-adoption semantics; **the vote slot + signer state + outbox as one
   273	   transaction** (a half-durable vote slot is _worse_ than none — it enables double-signing); the adoption
   274	   pointer swap; latched-ACL genesis semantics.
   275	8. **Shadow before destructive**, and **observation before acting**. Snapshots are produced, verified and
   276	   digest-compared across independent replicas plus archival replay before anything is pruned; seal computes
   277	   and compares cuts before it certifies them.
   278	9. **Extend the existing test muscle.** `packages/test-utils/src/property-harness.ts` (seeded mulberry32,
   279	   fake-timer virtual clock), the `linearize-reference.test.ts` independent-oracle pattern, the proptest
   280	   convergence/partition suites, `perf-contracts.test.ts`'s instrumented-probe-counter pattern, the
   281	   `failure-campaign` harness. A gate that does not run in CI will rot.
   282	10. **Scale is stated as per-object ceilings, in a profile table, bound to a named harness.** Anything not
   283	    in a profile table is not a supported scale claim.
   284	11. **P2P-first: every trust profile has a working zero-infrastructure configuration.** Operator-run nodes
   285	    (relay / mirror / signer, and optionally attestor later) are opt-in and additive — one way to obtain
   286	    durability or fanout, never the definition of either and never a requirement. A slice that makes any
   287	    profile depend on operator infrastructure to _exist_ is a regression against this principle (the
   288	    zero-deploy invariant, §0.5, is the Train-C instance of the same rule).

   402	### 2.4 Three live defects in the reference, confirmed by execution here
   403	
   404	These would be inherited by a faithful port. All three were found by review and re-verified by me directly.
   405	
   406	**D1 — `localeCompare` in three consensus-critical sorts is a fork vector.**
   407	`protocol.js:63` sorts the signer set (feeding `signerSetDigest`, which is in the anchor preimage at
   408	`protocol.js:199`); `seal.js:77` sorts QC votes before the QC digest; `archive.js:163` sorts archive-index
   409	entries before the Merkle root. `localeCompare` with no locale argument uses the host's ICU data. Measured:
   410	
   411	```
   412	ids            = ['peer-B','peer-a','Peer-a','peer_a','peerä']
   413	localeCompare  → peer_a, peer-a, Peer-a, peer-B, peerä
   414	codepoint      → Peer-a, peer-B, peer-a, peer_a, peerä
   415	```
   416	
   417	Two replicas with different default locales compute different `signerSetDigest` → different anchor hash →
   418	**permanent fork**, or two disjoint quorums certifying different anchors for the same cut.
   419	_Resolution:_ UTF-8 byte order equals codepoint order, not UTF-16 code-unit order. All protocol sorts use
   420	that order, fixed per field in the registry as `sortRule: "codepoint"`. The registry also constrains the `signerId` charset (no control
   421	characters), which additionally closes the `\0` key-smuggling in the NUL-delimited vote key
   422	(`seal.js:264`, `indexeddb-store.js:37`) — replaced by native IDB array keys.
   423	
   424	**D2 — `Float32Array` `-0` encodes to bytes the reference's own decoder rejects.** Measured:
   425	
   426	```
   427	encodeCanonical(Float32Array.of(-0))  → 0b0180000000        (succeeds)
   428	decodeCanonical(0b0180000000)         → throws "typed array contains non-canonical negative zero"
   429	encode(f32 -0) === encode(f32 +0)     → false
   430	```
   431	
   432	The encoder normalizes `-0` for `number` (`canonical.js:104`) and `Float64Array` (`:127`) but **not**
   433	`Float32Array` (`:121`); the decoder rejects `-0` in any typed array (`:357`). `Float32Array` is the tag
   434	aimed squarely at game state. A physics field that ever produces `-0` (trivially: `0 * -1`) exports a
   435	snapshot **no conforming peer can decode** — a room-wide unrecoverable close failure.
   436	_Resolution:_ registry amendment — the encoder MUST normalize `-0 → 0` in `Float32Array`.
   437	
   438	**D3 — admission verifies the digest before the cheap identity checks.** `admission.js:44-50` canonically
   439	encodes and SHA-256s the vertex _before_ comparing `objectId`/`protocolMajor`/`epoch`, so a flood of
   440	wrong-room garbage costs full crypto per message — violating spec §18.3's "reject oversize input before deep

   462	### 2.6 Crypto profile: sync `@noble/hashes`, and why §19's benchmark narrative is an artifact
   463	
   464	The reference is async-poisoned end to end because `subtle.digest` is Promise-only (`hash.js:55-58`):
   465	admission, vertex creation, Merkle append and QC building are all `async` **purely for hashing**, which also
   466	forces a top-level `await` into `ct-merkle.js:3`. The repo already ships sync SHA-256 everywhere
   467	(`packages/utils/src/hash/index.ts:1`; `@noble/hashes` is a production dependency of `object`, `utils`,
   468	`keychain`).
   469	
   470	AHE §19's slowest number — compact-accumulator Merkle at **739.8 ms median / 8192 leaves** — is dominated by
   471	~16k awaited WebCrypto round-trips over 64-byte inputs, not by hashing. In-browser runs here completed 2048
   472	appends in **50–87 ms** even under WebCrypto. So §19's "pure-JS Merkle is the slowest path, consider WASM"
   473	guidance is an artifact of the reference's crypto binding, not a property of the algorithm — and it must not
   474	be used as a sizing input.
   475	
   476	_Decision:_ all protocol digests are **sync**, over `@noble/hashes/sha2`, behind one
   477	`hashDomain(domain, ...parts): Uint8Array` in `@ts-drp/canonical`, preserving the reference's exact framing
   478	bytes. Ed25519 identity and seal signatures are likewise sync over `@noble/curves/ed25519.js`; their
   479	protocol functions return `Uint8Array`/`boolean` with no Promise surface. WebCrypto remains the custody
   480	backend for non-extractable browser seal keys, not the protocol verification backend. `worker-host` MAY
   481	eventually own the boundary for a bulk async backend for large snapshot/archive payloads, but that boundary
   482	ownership is **not** a Phase 2f closure requirement. Do not add a placeholder backend until a merged
   483	production UI-thread consumer exists and its exact representative payload measures release-matrix p95
   484	latency of at least 50 ms. That trigger opens a new TDD contract which preserves the canonical sync owner
   485	and proves equality on shared vectors. Re-benchmark in-repo after the golden paths before considering WASM;
   486	prefer established prior art when it fits rather than inventing a new implementation.

   489	
   490	`packages/types/src/proto/drp/v1/object.proto:7-19` carries operations as `google.protobuf.Value`, which
